title: The lithium balance: designing a cell forwards
lead: Most of us take cells apart backwards, from the OCV to the electrodes. Built forwards, the balance gets simple.
llms: The lithium balance of a cell in equilibrium: voltage window, N/P ratio, N/Li ratio including formation and prelithiation, aging modes and blended electrodes, each with a small interactive tool.

tabs.name: Voltage window
tabs.teaser: Why the cell voltage is a height difference, and what Vmin and Vmax cut out of the tanks.

tabs.name: N/P ratio
tabs.teaser: Why the anode is built bigger, and the more honest way to measure the margin to plating.

tabs.name: N/Li ratio
tabs.teaser: Why the cathode's first-cycle loss is no loss in the full cell, why most cells end up short of lithium, not of room, and what prelithiation does to that.

tabs.name: Aging
tabs.teaser: Why aging losses don't add up, and why a cell can lose active material without losing capacity.

tabs.name: Blends
tabs.teaser: Silicon and graphite as two connected tanks: where the kink in the curve comes from, and how dQ/dV takes a blend apart.
